subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the position vector of the point C on AB produced such that AC = 3AB, where a and b are the position vectors of A and B respectively.

mark_split.label: Write the given in position vectors
Solve for the position vector of C

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.61, chapter 6 ADDITION OF VECTORS, Very Short Answer question 12. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 shape is the one this bank uses for a Maths-1A Section A question: the first mark is for turning AC = 3AB into one equation in position vectors, the second for solving that equation. This book prints almost no exam-appearance years, so appearances[] is empty — Addition of Vectors has long been examined, we simply have no sourced years for this question. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1 to Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The answer 3b − 2a was checked a second way on a number line: taking a = 0 and b = 1 gives c = 3, and then AC = 3 and AB = 1, so AC = 3AB with C beyond B. The coefficients 3 and −2 add to 1, which is the test for C lying on the line AB.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the position vector of a point placed along AB produced.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the given in position vectors
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write both AB and AC head minus tail from the same point A. That turns the sentence 'AC = 3AB' into one equation with c as the only unknown.
steps.memory_tip: Write both vectors head minus tail from A: AB = b − a and AC = c − a. Then the given sentence is one equation in c.
lines: Let O be the origin and let c be the
AB = b − a and AC = c − a

recall.must_convey: That AB = b − a, AC = c − a, and the given condition becomes c − a = 3(b − a).
accept: AB is b minus a and AC is c minus a so c minus a equals three times b minus a
write both from A and put the condition as an equation
call the position vector of C as c and use head minus tail
AB equals b minus a, AC equals c minus a ani rasi equation cheyyali
set c minus a equal to three b minus a

steps.why: The condition is about the vectors AB and AC, so both must be written from the same starting point A before the unknown c can appear in a single equation.
common_mistakes: Writing AC as a − c, which reverses the direction.
Multiplying only b by 3 and leaving the a alone.

steps.label: Solve for the position vector of C
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Expand the bracket and collect the a terms. Two of the three a terms cancel, leaving −2a, and the coefficients 3 and −2 add to 1.
steps.memory_tip: The coefficients of a and b must add to 1 for C to be on the line AB: 3 + (−2) = 1.

accept: expand and bring the a across to get three b minus two a
the position vector of C is three b minus two a
c equals three b minus two a

collect the a terms and finish with three b minus two a

steps.why: AB produced means C lies beyond B on the same straight line, and 3b − 2a is three times as far from A as B is, in the same direction. The coefficients adding to 1 is the check that the point is on that line.
common_mistakes: Stopping at 3b − 3a and losing the +a brought across.
Answering 3b, which is not on the line AB in general.
